headline: Nous Research, an open-source AI developer, has raised $90 million to bring its Hermes AI agent to businesses.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: the funding is reported by the WSJ and its details are consistent across the copies read; usage figures are left out as unchecked.
importance_line: It gives companies a funded open-source option for keeping their data in-house, though Dillon Rolnick, chief executive of Nous Research, himself calls $90 million modest by current AI funding standards.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that Nous Research raised $90 million at a $1.5 billion valuation. Ventureburn says the money will turn its open-source Hermes agent into an enterprise product that companies can run locally or in the cloud, keeping their data private, with Nvidia, Microsoft's M12 fund, Samsung and Y Combinator among the investors.
notes: WSJ blocked here (401, paywall). Facts read in Ventureburn's write-up, which does not name the WSJ. WSJ credit: its own exclusive (7 Oct 2026) and the CryptoRank and Dealroom headlines that cite the WSJ. Left out as unchecked company claims: 24 million clones and about 2.5% of global token usage.
